money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Omani Rial (OMR). Declare all precious metals, local and foreign currency valued OMR6000 or more when you arrive and depart. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. More information is available here: Traveller Services You can easily exchange US dollars and euros at commercial banks and currency bureaus. Credit card facilities and ATMs are widely available. Ask your bank if your cards will work in Oman.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include the death penalty. Possessing even a small amount of drugs can result in lengthy jail terms and heavy fines. These laws also apply if you're transiting through Oman. Police may detain you if you are accompanied by a person who is involved in drug cases, including trafficking, possessing or using drugs. You may remain in detention until investigations are concluded for all parties. If you come to the attention of the local authorities, they may require you to take a blood test, particularly if they suspect you have used drugs or alcohol. If you refuse, you could be arrested for your failure to comply.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: If you're involved in legal matters, get professional legal advice. This especially includes family law regarding divorce, child custody and child support. Know your rights and responsibilities. Authorities may not let you leave Oman if you: are involved in business or labour disputes have unpaid debts, and bills. Unpaid bills include: giving somebody a cheque which bounces (including post-dated and ‘security’ cheques) non-payment of bills (for example property rent, hotel bills or car hire). have unpaid traffic fines. You can check if you have outstanding traffic fines via the ROP app or online service: Royal Oman Police Website - Online Services - Traffic Offense Payment. have legal procee
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal and may lead to severe punishment, including prison and fines. Cross-dressing is also illegal. If you're transgender or intersex, or your gender on your passport doesn't match your appearance, you may: be questioned at immigration be denied entry into Oman
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in Oman. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking (including water) and smoking may be illegal in public during the day. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: If you hold an Omani residence permit you'll need to obtain an Omani driver's licence to be able to drive in Oman. If you're in Oman on a visit visa, you should hold an International Driving Permit (IDP). Your IDP should be endorsed by the Oman road authorities. This is usually done at the rental car company at the airport.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Press reports (Oman Observer) say the Civil Aviation Authority suspended all drone operating permits until further notice. Check the current status with the CAA before bringing or flying a drone.
laws.heading: Drone permits suspension

laws.rule: Travellers arriving or leaving must declare currency, bearer securities, banknotes, or precious metals or gemstones convertible to cash, above 6,000 Omani riyals. Customs duty exemptions on the page include gifts up to 300 riyals and 400 cigarettes.
laws.heading: Cash declaration and allowances

laws.rule: Customs lists a duty-free allowance of 2 litres of wine and 48 cans of beer for non-Muslim travellers; Muslims do not get the exemption. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says visitors may buy and drink alcohol in licensed venues such as hotels, restaurants and clubs, the minimum age is 21, and drinking or being drunk in public is an offence.
laws.heading: Alcohol

laws.rule: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs states that importing and using e-cigarettes is illegal in Oman.
laws.heading: E-cigarettes

laws.rule: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs advises asking permission before photographing people, and says photographing some government buildings or military sites is not allowed.
laws.heading: Photography

laws.rule: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says conservative dress is appreciated, especially at religious sites. In Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking in public in daylight hours are forbidden for Muslims and non-Muslims.
laws.heading: Dress and Ramadan

laws.rule: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says flying drones or remote-controlled flying devices without a valid licence is against the law. See also the separate entry on the current permit suspension.
laws.heading: Drone licence

laws.rule: Dimaniyat Islands Nature Reserve: apply electronically to the Environment Authority, pay electronically, await verification and receive the permit. Published conditions say entering or camping is prohibited from May to October. They do not clearly distinguish boat-only diving from landing; confirm the restriction for the planned activity rather than assuming a marine-access exemption.

Dimaniyat Islands: outside the restricted period, camping is confined to Al Jabal Al Kabeer and Al Joon, in Authority-designated places, with a maximum of 12 people or five tents. Barbecues are limited to designated sites there, and lights and fire must be out after 21:00. Do not touch or disturb nesting turtles or eggs, remove coral/marine life, bring plants/seeds/animals or interfere with fishing gear. These are named-reserve conditions, not a general Oman camping code.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Oman has strict Islamic dress and behaviour codes. Hotels may refuse accommodation to couples who can't prove they're married. You should contact your accommodation provider to seek clarification on the requirements. It is important to respect local customs and act in a culturally appropriate manner. Take extra care during Ramadan and Shia religious festivals. The Omani weekend is Friday and Saturday. To ensure you don't offend: avoid disrespecting Islam or any other religion avoid bad language, rude gestures and public displays of affection respect restrictions on alcohol and pork products. If in doubt, seek local advice. To observe dress codes: dress modestly in public when not at tourist  Experience Oman (Ministry of Heritage and Tourism) general guidelines: men and women should cover their shoulders and knees, especially in villages, reserves and cultural sites. Keep noise low and ask before photographing people or entering private property.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: CAR-102 requires registration of remote piloted aircraft above 250 g and sets operating limits. Press reports say the CAA suspended all drone permits (government, commercial and recreational) until further notice; the date and current status were not confirmed on a CAA page.

items.text: Not yet checked: any public CAA directory of drone operators.

CAR-102: all remote piloted aircraft except micro aircraft under 250 g are registered with the CAA before use. Flights stay in visual line of sight, at or below 400 ft AGL by day and 30 m from uninvolved people. Controlled airspace and areas within 5.5 km of a controlled aerodrome need specific approval.

Oman Observer (a newspaper, so a signal) reports that the CAA suspended all drone operating permits by circular from 3 March until further notice, and earlier reported 155 tourist green zones with an AirPass route for visitors. Check the CAA before relying on either report.
